test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Buses are Vans.

All Vans are Trucks.

Some Buses are Cars.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Trucks are Buses.

(II) Some Cars are Trucks.
solution:
**Given Statements:**

Some Buses are Vans.

All Vans are Trucks.

Some Buses are Cars.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/006a84ed0467efafd3eb81fcfc30fe370326067eca787bee6eeabb0da4ea9391.png] 

**Conclusion:**

(I) Some Trucks are Buses → **TRUE **(Those trucks which are Vans are also bus, so Some Trucks are Buses).

(II) Some Cars are Trucks → **FALSE **(There is no definite relation given between Cars and Trucks, so it can be possible only).

So, Only conclusion (I) follows.

Hence, the correct answer is ***"Option 3".***
